evidence.claim: Reuters described Benjamin Diokno as a two-time budget minister who would lead Marcos's economic team, Arsenio Balisacan as returning as planning chief, and Felipe Medalla as incoming central bank governor, indicating a technocratic core for the new administration.
evidence.title: Factbox-Key figures in Philippine President Marcos' administration
evidence.excerpt: Reuters described Benjamin Diokno as a two-time budget minister who would lead Marcos's economic team, Arsenio Balisacan as returning as planning chief, and Felipe Medalla as incoming central bank governor, indicating a technocratic core for the new administration.
evidence.source_locator: search result excerpt under Benjamin Diokno, Arsenio Balisacan, and Felipe Medalla
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters factbox with named appointments and role descriptions; independent and specific to the 2022 transition.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers pre-inauguration 2022 appointments that shaped the target-year economic team.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's cabinet choices.
contrary_evidence: Competence is inferred from resumes, not proven by 2022 outcomes.
The broader cabinet still mixed technocrats with political figures.

evidence.claim: Diokno said the Marcos administration's first Medium-Term Fiscal Framework was aimed at reducing the deficit, promoting fiscal sustainability, and enabling robust growth.
evidence.title: Diokno bares six-year plan for fiscal stability and economic development
evidence.excerpt: Diokno said the Marcos administration's first Medium-Term Fiscal Framework was aimed at reducing the deficit, promoting fiscal sustainability, and enabling robust growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official announcement of a dated fiscal plan with explicit targets.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and about the administration's medium-term plan.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the administration level, though the source is still a plan rather than execution.
contrary_evidence: Plan stage only; implementation and results are not established here.
Growth outcomes also depended on inherited post-pandemic recovery.

evidence.claim: The IMF said a new administration took office in July with a blueprint for an inclusive, sustainable, and green recovery, but the economy still faced the need for the right policy mix, stronger fiscal buffers, and higher long-term growth.
evidence.title: Philippines: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said a new administration took office in July with a blueprint for an inclusive, sustainable, and green recovery, but the economy still faced the need for the right policy mix, stronger fiscal buffers, and higher long-term growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral assessment with an explicit policy diagnosis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Marcos's policy direction after July 2022; macro outcomes also reflected inherited fundamentals and global shocks.
contrary_evidence: Inflation and fiscal space had deteriorated by late 2022.
The report also says the outlook was challenged by a difficult global environment.

evidence.claim: Before Marcos took office, BSP raised the policy rate to 2.25 percent and projected 2022 inflation above target at 4.6 percent, citing food, energy, and supply pressures.
evidence.title: Monetary Policy Report May 2022
evidence.excerpt: Before Marcos took office, BSP raised the policy rate to 2.25 percent and projected 2022 inflation above target at 4.6 percent, citing food, energy, and supply pressures.
evidence.source_locator: Monetary Policy Summary and Economic Outlook
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official monetary policy report with explicit forecast and policy action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited baseline only; not attributable to Marcos.
contrary_evidence: This source predates Marcos's June 30 inauguration.
It reflects inherited inflation pressures rather than Marcos policy.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that BSP raised rates by 75 basis points off-cycle to contain broadening inflationary pressure and rescue a faltering peso.
evidence.title: Philippine central bank hastens interest rate rise, ready for more action
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that BSP raised rates by 75 basis points off-cycle to contain broadening inflationary pressure and rescue a faltering peso.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a specific, dated policy action and motive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: monetary policy was central-bank action, but it responded to the macro environment the Marcos administration faced.
contrary_evidence: The move was by the independent central bank, not the president directly.
It shows crisis management more than a Marcos-originated policy.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said the Philippines was poised to grow 5.7 percent in 2022 and that continuity of growth- and investment-supporting policies was key to strengthening recovery.
evidence.title: Philippines Economic Updates
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said the Philippines was poised to grow 5.7 percent in 2022 and that continuity of growth- and investment-supporting policies was key to strengthening recovery.
evidence.source_locator: June 2022 entry on the economic updates page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral growth forecast and policy assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly baseline and partly policy-continuity advice; not a direct score of Marcos's implementation.
contrary_evidence: Growth forecast was based on domestic recovery conditions that predated the administration.
The report also notes external and global uncertainty.

evidence.claim: NEDA said the Marcos administration's 8-point socioeconomic agenda would address short-term inflation and shock vulnerability, and longer-term job creation, infrastructure, logistics, energy, digitalization, regulation, and governance.
evidence.title: NEDA to flesh out development agenda for addressing constraints to inclusive growth
evidence.excerpt: NEDA said the Marcos administration's 8-point socioeconomic agenda would address short-term inflation and shock vulnerability, and longer-term job creation, infrastructure, logistics, energy, digitalization, regulation, and governance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official release quoting NEDA's implementation agenda and priorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the administration level.
contrary_evidence: It is an agenda statement, not implementation.
The source is official and promotional.

evidence.claim: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that his administration would fight food-price spikes by increasing production and supporting consumers' purchasing power.
evidence.title: Marcos relays food production agenda in 1st SONA
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that his administration would fight food-price spikes by increasing production and supporting consumers' purchasing power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential directive within the target year, reported on an official agency page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct.
contrary_evidence: The source is self-reporting and policy intent, not implementation.
The food-price problem was partly inherited and global.

evidence.claim: The Marcos administration's first approved appropriations law increased funding for education, agriculture for food security, health, labor and employment, tourism, public works, and energy.
evidence.title: Senate approves 2023 national budget on third reading
evidence.excerpt: The Marcos administration's first approved appropriations law increased funding for education, agriculture for food security, health, labor and employment, tourism, public works, and energy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific budget allocation with executive attribution and concrete sectoral priorities.
evidence.period_fit: Passed in 2022 as the first budget under Marcos for FY2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the administration level; implementation follows later.
contrary_evidence: Budget approval does not prove spending quality or execution.
Some increases mainly continue existing programs.

evidence.claim: DOF said the Marcos administration had streamlined private-sector participation through amended investment laws and revised BOT rules to make PPPs more attractive and to secure domestic and foreign investment.
evidence.title: Marcos admin streamlines private sector participation processes to encourage investments
evidence.excerpt: DOF said the Marcos administration had streamlined private-sector participation through amended investment laws and revised BOT rules to make PPPs more attractive and to secure domestic and foreign investment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific administration policy and implementation step, dated in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the administration level, though the law changes partly built on prior reforms.
contrary_evidence: The source is official and promotional.
Implementation benefits were projected, not yet fully evidenced.

evidence.claim: DOF said the Marcos administration's MTFF included real-property valuation reform to broaden the tax base and promote a just, equitable, and efficient valuation system.
evidence.title: DOF unveils fiscal priority reforms under Marcos admin
evidence.excerpt: DOF said the Marcos administration's MTFF included real-property valuation reform to broaden the tax base and promote a just, equitable, and efficient valuation system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Explicit reform text tied to the administration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the administration level.
contrary_evidence: Proposed reform only; not proof of enactment or anti-corruption impact.
The source is a ministry announcement.

evidence.claim: PSA said StatDev 2022 showed the Philippines made progress on some development goals, with only four of 15 sectoral chapters at average performance and six of nine core indicators meeting targets.
evidence.title: PSA releases the 2022 Statistical Indicators on Philippine Development
evidence.excerpt: PSA said StatDev 2022 showed the Philippines made progress on some development goals, with only four of 15 sectoral chapters at average performance and six of nine core indicators meeting targets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistical synthesis with year-specific targets and outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed: combines inherited conditions and Marcos-year implementation; not a direct causal estimate.
contrary_evidence: The same summary says many indicators were still off track.
It is an aggregate planning metric, not a ruler-specific causal estimate.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said the Philippines was poised to grow 5.7 percent in 2022, warned that inflation was a pressing concern, and said policy continuity, targeted social assistance, and support for agriculture would matter for recovery.
evidence.title: Continuity of Policies Supporting Growth and Investments Key to Strengthen Recovery in the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said the Philippines was poised to grow 5.7 percent in 2022, warned that inflation was a pressing concern, and said policy continuity, targeted social assistance, and support for agriculture would matter for recovery.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank country press release with explicit dated macro assessment and policy recommendations.
evidence.period_fit: In-period baseline and early-2022 context for the Marcos transition.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited and external context; useful as a starting condition rather than proof of Marcos execution.
contrary_evidence: The piece is a forecast and policy note, not a measurement of Marcos-administered delivery.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Benjamin Diokno would lead the Marcos economic team as finance secretary, Arsenio Balisacan would return as planning chief, and Felipe Medalla would replace Diokno at the BSP.
evidence.title: Factbox-Key figures in Philippine President Marcos' administration
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Benjamin Diokno would lead the Marcos economic team as finance secretary, Arsenio Balisacan would return as planning chief, and Felipe Medalla would replace Diokno at the BSP.
evidence.source_locator: factbox entries for Diokno, Balisacan, and Medalla
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent wire, though the page is syndicated through MarketScreener.
evidence.period_fit: In-period; appointments were announced before Marcos was sworn in.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because these were his cabinet/economic-team selections.
contrary_evidence: Experienced appointments do not by themselves prove better execution or coordination.

evidence.claim: Marcos's first EO reorganized the Office of the President, abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and the Office of the Cabinet Secretary, and said the administration sought simplicity, economy, and efficiency in the bureaucracy.
evidence.title: Executive Order No. 1
evidence.excerpt: Marcos's first EO reorganized the Office of the President, abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and the Office of the Cabinet Secretary, and said the administration sought simplicity, economy, and efficiency in the bureaucracy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary legal text signed by the president on his first day in office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as a signed executive action.
contrary_evidence: Abolishing PACC can be read as streamlining, but also as reducing a specialized anti-corruption channel, so the net effect is ambiguous.

evidence.claim: Marcos's first SONA asked Congress to pass 19 priority measures, including National Government Rightsizing, Budget Modernization, E-Government, and E-Governance, to improve government services.
evidence.title: PBBM urges Congress to pass admin’s 19 priority measures
evidence.excerpt: Marcos's first SONA asked Congress to pass 19 priority measures, including National Government Rightsizing, Budget Modernization, E-Government, and E-Governance, to improve government services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential communications release summarizing the president's own SONA agenda.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because it is his own legislative agenda and public instruction to Congress.
contrary_evidence: The measures still required congressional passage and later administrative follow-through.

evidence.claim: Marcos set numeric medium-term goals for GDP growth, poverty reduction, debt reduction, and upper-middle-income status, and said the MTFF would anchor annual spending and financing plans.
evidence.title: State of the Nation Address of His Excellency Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. President of the Philippines to the Congress of the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: Marcos set numeric medium-term goals for GDP growth, poverty reduction, debt reduction, and upper-middle-income status, and said the MTFF would anchor annual spending and financing plans.
evidence.source_locator: MTFF bullet list and the paragraph beginning 'The aforementioned headline goals summarize...'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct transcript of the president's own address and targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because these are his announced goals and fiscal architecture.
contrary_evidence: Targets are commitments, not proof of execution.

evidence.claim: The Marcos administration submitted a PHP 5.268 trillion FY2023 budget prioritizing education, infrastructure, health, agriculture, and social safety nets, with explicit sectoral increases.
evidence.title: DBM submits 2023 Budget to Congress; Education, infrastructure, health, social protection, agriculture, top budget priorities
evidence.excerpt: The Marcos administration submitted a PHP 5.268 trillion FY2023 budget prioritizing education, infrastructure, health, agriculture, and social safety nets, with explicit sectoral increases.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Budget department release with concrete allocations and named priority sectors.
evidence.period_fit: In-period; submitted in August 2022 for the 2023 budget cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos through his administration's budget proposal and priority-setting.
contrary_evidence: The budget is a plan and appropriation proposal; delivery still depends on execution by agencies and Congress.

evidence.claim: Marcos presented the eight-point socioeconomic agenda to investors, saying it would address inflation and food security in the near term and jobs, infrastructure, human capital, digitalization, innovation, and livable communities over the medium term.
evidence.title: Road to progress: PBBM touts eight-point socio-economic agenda before US investors, biz leaders
evidence.excerpt: Marcos presented the eight-point socioeconomic agenda to investors, saying it would address inflation and food security in the near term and jobs, infrastructure, human capital, digitalization, innovation, and livable communities over the medium term.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted summary of the agenda
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official release summarizing the president's own public presentation to investors.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because it is his own public articulation of the governing program.
contrary_evidence: Investor-facing rhetoric can overstate readiness and does not itself prove implementation.

evidence.claim: Marcos led the oath-taking of reappointed and ad interim cabinet members including Benjamin Diokno, Arsenio Balisacan, Alfredo Pascual, Renato Solidum Jr., Raphael Lotilla, and others.
evidence.title: PBBM leads oath-taking of Cabinet members in Malacañang
evidence.excerpt: Marcos led the oath-taking of reappointed and ad interim cabinet members including Benjamin Diokno, Arsenio Balisacan, Alfredo Pascual, Renato Solidum Jr., Raphael Lotilla, and others.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential release listing the actual appointees sworn into office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as the appointing authority.
contrary_evidence: Cabinet swearing-in does not itself prove effective coordination or delivery.

evidence.claim: Marcos said he would issue an EO imposing a one-year moratorium on land amortization and interest for agrarian reform beneficiaries and said this would help farmers invest in their farms and support food security.
evidence.title: Marcos Jr.: Agrarian reform program must continue
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said he would issue an EO imposing a one-year moratorium on land amortization and interest for agrarian reform beneficiaries and said this would help farmers invest in their farms and support food security.
evidence.source_locator: article body quoting the first SONA commitment and EO 4 rationale
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official release linking a promised policy to a later presidential order and explaining its purpose.
evidence.period_fit: In-period; October 2022 follow-through on a July 2022 commitment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as a signed executive action.
contrary_evidence: This is a sector-specific measure; it does not by itself show broad economic competence.
The effects would take time and depend on administrative rollout.

evidence.claim: The Marcos administration said it had streamlined private-sector participation through amended investment laws and revised BOT rules to attract more domestic and foreign investment and make PPPs more attractive.
evidence.title: Marcos admin streamlines private sector participation processes to encourage investments
evidence.excerpt: The Marcos administration said it had streamlined private-sector participation through amended investment laws and revised BOT rules to attract more domestic and foreign investment and make PPPs more attractive.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official finance-ministry release describing enacted or operationalized investment reforms and their intended purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partially attributable to Marcos; some reforms were inherited or legislated earlier, but the administration is claiming operational ownership and sequencing.
contrary_evidence: Some of the enabling laws were passed before Marcos took office, so not all credit belongs to him.
Claims about improved investor response are forward-looking rather than outcome proof.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the new administration had a blueprint for an inclusive, sustainable, and green recovery, but still faced three challenges: choosing the right policy mix for recovery and price stability, building fiscal buffers, and raising long-term growth.
evidence.title: Philippines: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the new administration had a blueprint for an inclusive, sustainable, and green recovery, but still faced three challenges: choosing the right policy mix for recovery and price stability, building fiscal buffers, and raising long-term growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent IMF country report with a clear summary of the administration's stated blueprint and macro tasks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Marcos's administration because the report describes its own blueprint and policy challenge set.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also implies the blueprint was still at the challenge-setting stage rather than proven execution.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said the Philippines was poised to grow 5.7 percent in 2022 and that inflation, global shocks, and the need for continuity in pro-growth and investment policies shaped the recovery outlook.
evidence.title: Continuity of Policies Supporting Growth and Investments Key to Strengthen Recovery in the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said the Philippines was poised to grow 5.7 percent in 2022 and that inflation, global shocks, and the need for continuity in pro-growth and investment policies shaped the recovery outlook.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent country press release with specific macro forecast and policy context.
evidence.period_fit: In-period baseline and early-2022 macro context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited and external context; not a direct measure of Marcos execution.
contrary_evidence: The piece does not evaluate Marcos's own implementation, only the environment he inherited.

evidence.claim: The PSA said GDP grew 7.6 percent in 2022 and unemployment fell to 5.4 percent, but only four of 15 sectoral chapters had average performance and several development targets were still unmet.
evidence.title: PSA releases the 2022 Statistical Indicators on Philippine Development
evidence.excerpt: The PSA said GDP grew 7.6 percent in 2022 and unemployment fell to 5.4 percent, but only four of 15 sectoral chapters had average performance and several development targets were still unmet.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistical release with the annual 2022 scorecard and target comparisons.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Marcos-era execution, but also to post-pandemic rebound and inherited trend effects.
contrary_evidence: The same release notes mixed performance across sectors and unmet targets, so it does not prove broad execution success.

evidence.claim: The BSP table shows annual average inflation of 5.8 percent in 2022 and December 2022 inflation of 8.1 percent.
evidence.title: Inflation Rates
evidence.excerpt: The BSP table shows annual average inflation of 5.8 percent in 2022 and December 2022 inflation of 8.1 percent.
evidence.source_locator: Table 34, rows for annual average and December 2022
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official BSP statistical table with clear annual and monthly inflation data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the Marcos administration's macro management, but heavily affected by global and inherited price shocks.
contrary_evidence: Inflation is not solely caused by the ruler; global food, fuel, and supply shocks were major contributors.

evidence.claim: At its November 17, 2022 meeting, the BSP raised the overnight reverse repurchase rate to 5.0 percent and revised inflation forecasts to 5.8 percent for 2022 and 4.3 percent for 2023.
evidence.title: Monetary Policy Report November 2022
evidence.excerpt: At its November 17, 2022 meeting, the BSP raised the overnight reverse repurchase rate to 5.0 percent and revised inflation forecasts to 5.8 percent for 2022 and 4.3 percent for 2023.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official central-bank policy summary with explicit rate decision and forecast revisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly an independent BSP response, not direct presidential action, but it reflects the macro conditions the administration faced.
contrary_evidence: The BSP action is not a direct Marcos decision, so it can only be used as macro context and policy-environment corroboration.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said strong domestic demand was driving growth, but high inflation and rising rates would slow the economy and could worsen child malnutrition and learning losses unless policy focused on health, education, and agriculture.
evidence.title: Opening remarks at the launch of the Philippines Economic Update December 2022 Edition
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said strong domestic demand was driving growth, but high inflation and rising rates would slow the economy and could worsen child malnutrition and learning losses unless policy focused on health, education, and agriculture.
evidence.source_locator: opening remarks lines 24-38 and the later policy-focus paragraph
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent World Bank remarks summarizing the December 2022 outlook and risks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Marcos-era policy choices, but also heavily shaped by post-pandemic rebound and global slowdown.
contrary_evidence: This is still an outlook note, not a direct measure of implementation success.
Some growth and demand strength were inherited recovery effects rather than direct new-policy output.

evidence.claim: Government agencies had used 94% of the P4.01 trillion in Notices of Cash Allocation issued in the first 11 months of 2022, leaving P257.94 billion unused, up from 91% a year earlier.
evidence.title: Gov’t agencies’ cash usage hits 94% at end of Nov.
evidence.excerpt: Government agencies had used 94% of the P4.01 trillion in Notices of Cash Allocation issued in the first 11 months of 2022, leaving P257.94 billion unused, up from 91% a year earlier.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent business reporting citing DBM data, with explicit figures and comparison to the prior year.
evidence.period_fit: In-period; late-2022 execution metric for the Marcos administration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Marcos through administration-level spending control, but also affected by inherited budget processes and election-ban timing.
contrary_evidence: This is a cash-utilization measure, not a direct output or welfare outcome measure.
It does not isolate Marcos-specific agency performance from pre-existing spending momentum.

evidence.claim: In MIMAROPA, 97.2% of families with children aged 6-11 had children in Grade 1-6 in 2022, and 90.1% of families with children aged 12-15 had children in junior high school.
evidence.title: Highlights of the 2022 Annual Poverty Indicators Survey (APIS): Education
evidence.publisher: Philippine Statistics Authority, MIMAROPA regional office
evidence.excerpt: In MIMAROPA, 97.2% of families with children aged 6-11 had children in Grade 1-6 in 2022, and 90.1% of families with children aged 12-15 had children in junior high school.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official PSA regional APIS release using household survey data, with explicit percentages and year reference.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2024 reporting on 2022 household survey data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: these are regional household outcomes during Marcos's first year, but they are not uniquely attributable to his choices without additional causal isolation.
contrary_evidence: Regional figures do not establish national performance.
They reflect a single region and a household survey, so they are informative but not comprehensive.

evidence.claim: In MIMAROPA, 24.8% of families were beneficiaries of 4Ps, 12.1% received AICS, and 84.8% had at least one member/dependent/beneficiary of PhilHealth in 2022.
evidence.title: Highlights of the 2022 Annual Poverty Indicators Survey: Social Protection Programs
evidence.publisher: Philippine Statistics Authority, MIMAROPA regional office
evidence.excerpt: In MIMAROPA, 24.8% of families were beneficiaries of 4Ps, 12.1% received AICS, and 84.8% had at least one member/dependent/beneficiary of PhilHealth in 2022.
evidence.source_locator: social assistance and PhilHealth sections in the article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official PSA regional APIS release grounded in household survey data and reporting multiple program participation rates.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2024 reporting on 2022 household survey data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: the figures reflect program reach under the Marcos period, but the article does not isolate his personal contribution from inherited program design and regional administration.
contrary_evidence: Regional reach is not the same as quality or effectiveness of delivery.
The data are regional and do not show whether Marcos personally improved access beyond inherited systems.

evidence.claim: PSA reported that poverty incidence among families was 10.9% in 2023, and that the mean per capita income of families near the poverty line increased 22.9% from 2021 to 2023, producing a 2.3 percentage-point decline in family poverty incidence.
evidence.title: Percentage of Filipino Families Classified as Poor Declined to 10.9 percent in 2023
evidence.excerpt: PSA reported that poverty incidence among families was 10.9% in 2023, and that the mean per capita income of families near the poverty line increased 22.9% from 2021 to 2023, producing a 2.3 percentage-point decline in family poverty incidence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National statistical release with explicit poverty and income figures.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective follow-through beyond 2022; useful for trajectory but not a direct within-year 2022 outcome measure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Marcos-era policy and budget choices, but also heavily shaped by post-pandemic recovery and price dynamics.
contrary_evidence: This is 2023 outcome data, so it cannot be treated as a clean measure of 2022-only execution.
The release itself notes the decline is explained partly by threshold and income changes over time.

evidence.claim: PSA reported that 11 of 18 regions recorded statistically significant decreases in family poverty incidence in 2023 from 2021, while some regions saw increases or only non-significant downtrends.
evidence.title: 11 out of 18 Regions Recorded Significant Decreases in Poverty Incidence in 2023
evidence.excerpt: PSA reported that 11 of 18 regions recorded statistically significant decreases in family poverty incidence in 2023 from 2021, while some regions saw increases or only non-significant downtrends.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National statistics release with explicit regional poverty comparisons and significance language.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2024 regional follow-through on the 2022-2023 trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Marcos-era macro and social-policy choices, but also affected by inherited recovery patterns and regional heterogeneity.
contrary_evidence: This is a 2023 comparison against 2021, not a direct 2022 administration-only effect.
Some regions worsened, so the regional picture is mixed.

National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.
